body: Spacecraft propulsion traditionally relies on volatile fuels and separate, bulky systems for different types of maneuvering in space. NASA is working to change that paradigm. Engineers at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, recently completed a rigorous series of environmental and physical tests on a new small satellite designed to make spaceflight safer and more efficient. The ASCENT (Advanced Spacecraft Energetic Non-Toxic) Propulsion Dual Mode mission is a flight demonstration of a spacecraft about the size of a large shoebox. The mission will test a single, integrated propulsion system that uses a common fuel tank to feed two different types of engines. Dr. Nehemiah Williams, the demonstration’s project manager at NASA, prepares to start testing the mission’s flight hardware in a clean room at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama. The mission will demonstrate a single, non-toxic propulsion system that combines both high-thrust and low-thrust capabilities into a common tank. title: Where’s my timestamp? Google Messages is updating its UI, and users are confused
summary: Messages introduces new swipe controls for your chat's metadata.
body: TL;DR Back in 2024, Google first started working on swipe gestures to view timestamps in Messages. That new interface is now widely rolling out to users. Messages also now supports swiping right to directly reply. When you’re looking back on your text message history, it’s not just the texts and the GIFs you care about. The metadata also tells a story, too: when messages were sent, if they went out with encryption, and whether or not they were even received. If you’re opening up Google Messages this week but suddenly are having trouble finding some of those details, worry not — Google’s just tweaking how you access them. So far, when you’ve gone to tap on a message in your chat history, Messages would pull up its metadata right below: timestamp, delivery status, encryption — the works. But 9to5Google has now spotted a new design that’s been rolling out to more and more users, changing up how we see this info — and it’s not without its improvements.

As a spiral galaxy like our own Milky Way galaxy, NGC 4698 has spiral arms that curl around within a thin disk of stars, gas, and dust. These arms are marked by opaque clumps of brown dust and dotted with small collections of bright blue stars. Unlike many other spiral galaxies, NGC 4698’s delicate spiral arms are only prominent in the outer reaches of the disk; spiral arms often wind down to the very center of a galaxy, but NGC 4698’s spiral arms appear to shy away from its glowing center. title: Your Pixel Watch now flags your risk of hypertension and diabetes

body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel Watch 3 and newer models are receiving the promised Health Guardian features. These include blood pressure and insulin resistance trends, as well as sleep quality analysis. The features are now available for free on the Pixel Watch, while Fitbit Air users will have to pay for them. At the launch of the Pixel Watch 5 , Google announced Health Guardian , a suite of features that detect trends from your health data and predict concerning physiologic changes, such as hypertension, diabetes, or sleep apnea. Google promised to roll it out “in fall,” and it’s now delivering on that commitment. Starting today, three vital Health Guardian features, including blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality, are now available for the Pixel Watch 3 and Watch 4, alongside the newly launched Pixel Watch 5. These three metrics join Breathing Emergency detection , which has been available on the Pixel Watch 4 and 5 since launch, but only in limited European countries.

title: Privacy Display on the Galaxy S27 Ultra could pick up this handy new trick
summary: Split-screen display dimming could make it to the early 2027 Samsung flagship.
body: TL;DR Prominent leaker Ice Universe claims the Galaxy S27 Ultra will introduce a split-screen Privacy Display feature, as seen on the Xiaomi 18 Pro series. This feature can cleverly dim just one app window in split-screen view, even when it’s resized. While Xiaomi appears to have more features tied to this privacy feature, the leaker notes that Samsung still has the upper hand in overall dimming capacity. Samsung set the industry standard by introducing Privacy Display on the Galaxy S26 Ultra , which enables hardware-level screen dimming to shake off shoulder surfers. While some brands have already revealed their own take on this feature, the freshly announced Xiaomi 18 Pro series takes it to another level with Smart Privacy Display. We’re now learning that Samsung may introduce at least one of the Xiaomi flagship’s privacy-oriented features in its early 2027 smartphone. Writing on X, leaker Ice Universe claims the Xiaomi 18 Pro’s unique split-screen privacy protection system will make its way to the Galaxy S27 Ultra . This split-screen privacy mechanism cleverly dims only one app, even as you resize it, while keeping the other in its normal, visible state.

title: Gmail is turning its stars and importance markers blue, and users aren’t happy
summary: Google says the change helps with accessibility, but users complain it flattens hierarchy and clutters the inbox.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google replaced Gmail’s default yellow stars and yellow importance chevrons with high-contrast, saturated blue markers to improve accessibility. However, users complain that the identical blue tones flatten the visual hierarchy, make email scanning harder, and add visual clutter. While there’s no way to revert the changes, you can manually select a yellow star preset (and re-star items) or hide importance chevrons entirely in Settings. Google is rolling out a visual overhaul to Gmail on the web, replacing its longstanding yellow stars and importance markers with a bright, high-contrast blue. While Gmail has gained plenty of genuinely practical upgrades recently, such as letting you copy 2FA codes directly without opening emails or leveraging AI overview search capabilities , this particular color switch has annoyed desktop users who rely on quick visual cues to scan their messages. In a post on X , the official Gmail team confirmed the change, explaining that it updated the default star and “Important” label colors from yellow to blue to meet modern accessibility standards and ensure inboxes are easier to read and more inclusive.

title: Google Messages has a camera flash problem, and nobody knows why

body: TL;DR Multiple Google Messages users are having trouble with the timing of the LED flash when taking photos in chats. In some cases, the LED flash simply refuses to activate even when toggled manually, though it functions normally in other camera apps. Apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, and Google Messages , along with several others, offer a camera interface in the chat to capture and send media. It now looks like Google’s messaging app may be stumbling at this basic function in some situations. A Verizon-branded Galaxy S24 Ultra owner on Reddit says Google Messages refuses to activate the flash while capturing an image from the chat. title: Data privacy isn’t just for nerds — here’s why you should care too
summary: The more I see how my personal data is used across services, the more I want to guard my privacy.
body: A lot of times when I’ve mentioned moving to more privacy-focused apps and services, the reaction is more than a shrug — it’s a declaration that online privacy isn’t all that important. Most recently, at a tech event, I mentioned moving to Brave to avoid Google’s data collection and targeted advertising, and another attendee said that it’s just not important to them. That’s when I realized that there’s this general misunderstanding that prioritizing data privacy is the pastime of nerds and those prone to donning tin foil hats. I know I was someone who used to take a more laissez-faire approach to my online privacy. Years later, after grappling with the consequences of this, I feel that data privacy and data collection should be something everyone cares about.

title: Google just closed the gap between Gemini Notebooks and Docs
summary: Gemini can now use your research to draft documents in Google Docs.
body: TL;DR Gemini in Google Docs can now draw information from your curated Gemini Notebooks. This ensures Gemini’s responses are grounded in your research. It also provides inline citations when drafting documents in Google Docs so you can verify facts without switching tabs. Gemini in Google Docs has long been a helpful assistant. It can create audio summaries of long documents, make a boring document more interesting with images, charts, and diagrams, and even consistently write in your tone across documents. Now, Google is taking things a step further by giving Gemini in Google Docs access to your Gemini Notebooks to ground its writing in sources you select. Google announced today that Gemini Notebooks can now be used as a context source in Google Docs. This means you no longer have to manually switch between tabs to cross-verify information in drafts created by Gemini. Once you have your research organized in a Gemini Notebook, you can add it as a source in Docs, and Gemini will draw information from it when writing.

The new models are reaching Gemini Notebook and Google Vids, with both also available to developers through Google AI Studio and the Gemini API. AI voiceovers can read a script. But getting them to actually perform it with the right accent, pacing, emotion, pauses, and even the occasional sigh is another story. To address this, Google has spent weeks growing Gemini 3.8 from the original Gemini 3.8 Flash into new Live and Live Extended Thinking models . And now it wants the same family to act the part, with Gemini 3.8 Flash Text-To-Speech (TTS) and Flash-Lite TTS rolling out. The biggest change for users is control. title: GrapheneOS just confirmed its first supported non-Pixel phone
summary: GrapheneOS users are finally getting a serious alternative to Google’s Pixels.
body: TL;DR GrapheneOS has confirmed that the Motorola Signature 27 will be its first officially supported Motorola phone. The flagship fits GrapheneOS’s stated hardware requirements, including a top-end Snapdragon chip and long-term software support. The move gives GrapheneOS users a major alternative to Pixels as the project increasingly pushes beyond Google hardware and services. For years, wanting GrapheneOS meant accepting one hardware choice: you needed a Google Pixel. Motorola’s partnership with the privacy-focused project promised to break that lock-in, but until now, we didn’t know which phone would go first. Following this week’s Signature 27 unveiling , GrapheneOS has answered that question directly: Motorola’s new flagship will be the first phone supported under the partnership. The confirmation came after an X user asked whether the Signature 27 would support GrapheneOS. “Yes, that will be the initial supported phone. Wait for official news about it,” the project replied . That last sentence matters, since GrapheneOS has not yet announced when support will arrive or whether Motorola will offer the OS preinstalled.
